raw_text:
Review README.md and /src files for repository purpose/structure and update this overview.

Framework: .NET 10.0 (`net10.0`); latest C#; nullable and implicit usings enabled; TreatWarningsAsErrors globally (`TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`); XML warning 1591 suppressed via `NoWarn`.

Structure: `src/`, `tests/`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `Template.slnx`. Uses MSBuild Central Package Management (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`); versions belong in [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), and projects reference packages without versions. Add packages via `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />`.

Style: file-scoped namespaces (`namespace MyProject.Feature;`), 2-space indentation, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM, Allman braces; underscore camelCase private fields, PascalCase constants, `var` when apparent, `I` interfaces, `Async` methods. Always use `{}` except single-line exits (`return`, `throw`); `csharp_prefer_braces = true`; primary constructors preferred and ALWAYS assign to readonly fields; top-level statements preferred; prefer pattern matching; expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors, NOT methods. Run `dotnet format`; analyzers come from [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props); consider NSDepCop.

Configuration: use `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, `IConfiguration`, `IOptions<T>`, strongly typed settings, User Secrets. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, appropriate levels, context, structured logging; avoid sensitive data; correlation IDs when possible.

Security/validation: Follow OWASP guidelines for secure coding practices. Validate and sanitize all user inputs. Use parameterized queries or ORM features to prevent SQL injection. Implement proper authentication and authorization mechanisms. Use HTTPS for all communications. Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` non-UI; prefer `FluentValidation` for complex/UI validation. UI invalid inputs must produce user-friendly errors; non-UI invalid inputs must throw appropriate guard-clause exceptions. HTTP methods should return suitable status codes for non-success results.

Architecture/testing: Write unit testable code. Offer to add tests to generated code if applicable - place such tests in the `tests/` folder. Only test code that you control and that has business logic; do not test framework code. Focused classes/methods (<20 lines), DI, composition, async I/O, parameter objects over >4 arguments. Prefer REPR with FastEndpoints and DDD. Use `*Request`/`*Response`, `*Command`/`*Query`, DTOs (not domain entities), `*Details`/`*Summary`; avoid colocating interfaces/implementations.

New projects: production in `src/`, tests in `tests/`; tests use `xUnit`. Run `dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`. Use xUnit, Arrange-Act-Assert (whitespace only), feature-mirroring folders, no “Tests” class suffix (folder suffix allowed), `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`/`[InlineData]`, `ClassName_MethodName.cs`, sentence-like names, separate unit/integration projects/folders. Prefer NSubstitute and Shouldly; avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Documentation: Markdown, headings, syntax-highlighted snippets, linting; blank lines around lists/code listings.

Reference [.editorconfig](.editorconfig), [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props), [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), and [.gitignore](.gitignore).
